findings.title: Physics captures are emitted as an immediate burst, not at target_fps over duration_seconds
findings.detail: CaptureBounds.resolve derives frame_count from target_fps and duration_seconds, but the loop immediately invokes get_physics_capture_v1 for every frame. Neither target_fps nor duration_seconds affects scheduling after line 133, and no clock/sleeper is available in this layer. A 63-frame, 1-second capture therefore requests 70 63 times back-to-back, making the recorded temporal sequence unsuitable for the advertised sampling contract and defeating duration semantics. The focused tests assert count boundaries but do not distinguish burst capture from paced capture.
findings.requiredFix: Inject a monotonic clock and bounded sleeper (or pass a capture schedule from collect_rollouts), wait for each planned sample time, and add a deterministic test proving requests are spaced and total elapsed schedule equals the requested duration without real sleeps.

findings.title: Physics integration continues to enlarge an already oversized orchestration module
findings.detail: The changed file has 1,945 pure lines and this diff adds 187 lines. The new persistence/contract modules are a useful split, but collection, recovery, provenance, and contract assembly still accumulate in the existing god function/module. This violates the remove-ai-slops oversized-module perspective and raises future regression cost; it is not the direct cause of the temporal correctness failure.
findings.requiredFix: Move the remaining physics collection/recovery orchestration behind a focused module boundary before further behavior is added.
